# Corrext and generative AI. Useful for understanding, but binding documents need a framework

ChatGPT, Azure OpenAI GPT and Claude rephrase, summarise and explain a legal passage better than a conventional translation engine. This page sets out what they do well, and what they cannot prove on their own on a binding Swiss document.

Request a demo

## The short answer

Yes, a general-purpose LLM translates and rephrases a legal passage very well.

What it does not provide on its own: sourced Swiss terminology, a guaranteed legal reference, a review interface, a quote, and data processing in Switzerland. In Corrext, Azure OpenAI GPT and Claude remain available, under your organisation's governance.

No sourced Swiss terminology

A term is rendered plausibly, with nothing to show how the Federal Gazette or fedlex.admin.ch actually renders it. In Corrext, that is the job of Fast lookup CHnell.

No guarantee on legal references

An article, an abbreviation or a court can be produced with full confidence and still be wrong, with no warning sign in the answer.

No review interface

No validation chain: no review level, no legal translator to order, no certification possible. In Corrext, review is ordered in Translation projects.

## What general-purpose LLMs do remarkably well

They are the best tools legal experts have ever had for working on the meaning of a text. Saying so does not weaken our argument: it is the honest starting point for the comparison.

Rephrasing and simplifying

Turning a dense clause into a readable paragraph for a client who is not a legal expert, or the reverse, in the register requested.

Summarising and explaining

Bringing out the structure of a 50-page written submission, explaining a contractual mechanism, isolating each party's obligations.

Handling ambiguity

Offering several readings of an ambiguous wording and spelling out what separates them, where a conventional translation engine silently picks one.

Exploring drafts

Quickly producing several versions of a clause to feed an internal discussion, before settling on the version that will be negotiated.

## Twelve criteria, based on real work on a case file

What we say about general-purpose LLMs is limited to what is public and stable. They are generic models, remarkable with language. They have no sourced corpus of Swiss law and no integrated review or certification chain, and their consumer plans process documents outside Switzerland. In Corrext, Azure OpenAI GPT and Claude are configured as third-party engines hosted abroad.

## An example of an error, and the source that settles it

A banking law sentence, translated from French into Italian. ChatGPT keeps the French abbreviation of the Banking Act; LexMachina uses the one found in federal texts, and CHnell shows its source.

Source · French

L'établissement assujetti veille au respect du secret bancaire au sens de l'art. 47 LB. En cas de faillite de la banque, la liquidation suit les règles de la LP, sous réserve des dispositions de la LB.

ChatGPT

L’istituto assoggettato vigila sul rispetto del segreto bancario ai sensi dell’art. 47 LB. In caso di fallimento della banca, la liquidazione è disciplinata dalle norme della LEF, fatte salve le disposizioni della LB.

LexMachina

L’istituto assoggettato vigila sul rispetto del segreto bancario ai sensi dell’articolo 47 LBCR. In caso di fallimento della banca, la liquidazione è retta dalle disposizioni della LEF, fatte salve le disposizioni della LBCR.

### The proof, in CHnell

In Swiss Italian, the Banking Act is abbreviated as LBCR: ChatGPT keeps the French abbreviation, LexMachina uses the one found in federal texts, and CHnell shows its source.

Compare the engines on your own texts in the demo

- Real outputs recorded on 18 October 2026: ChatGPT on chatgpt.com, LexMachina in Corrext.

- In CHnell, 905 official segments from the Federal Gazette and fedlex.admin.ch align LBCR with LB.

- A one-off, dated example: judge for yourself on your own texts.

## Frequently asked questions about general-purpose LLMs and Swiss law

Can I use ChatGPT to translate a contract?

To understand a clause, grasp its scope or prepare a discussion, yes: a general-purpose LLM does this very well. For a contract that will be signed, sent to a third party or filed with an authority, no, not on its own. It provides no sourced Swiss terminology, no guarantee on legal references, no review by a legal translator and no data processing in Switzerland. In Corrext, these models remain available, but the binding version goes through Light, Full or Double review.

How do I check a Swiss legal reference?

Do not ask the engine that has just produced it: ask a source. In Corrext, highlight the term or abbreviation in the source text and click Fast Lookup. The CHnell concordancer displays aligned segments from official Swiss sources, with the domain, the source and a Show in context link. You then see how the term is actually rendered in the Federal Gazette or on fedlex.admin.ch, not how a model assumes it should be.

Does Corrext use general-purpose LLMs?

Yes. Azure OpenAI GPT and Claude are available in Corrext, alongside LexMachina and DeepL Pro, and you choose the engine each time you send a text. Because they are hosted abroad, selecting them triggers the Attorney-Client privilege notice, which restates your organisation's policy: full pseudonymisation, no sensitive matters. The Alternatives panel lets you compare their suggestions with the Swiss engine's on the same sentence.

Do general-purpose LLMs make up statutory provisions?

It can produce a reference, a court or a term that is plausible but wrong, and nothing in its answer flags the error. In the banking law sentence shown above, ChatGPT keeps the French abbreviation LB where the Italian versions of federal texts use LBCR. That is precisely why Corrext displays several alternatives, each labelled with its engine, and gives access to the concordancer.

Are my conversations with a consumer AI assistant confidential?

Terms vary from one provider and one plan to another, and they change. Two points remain constant for a Swiss law firm: the document is transferred outside Switzerland, and nothing in the interface reminds users what their internal policy requires before they send it. In Corrext, the Attorney-Client privilege notice appears when the engine is chosen, and Highly sensitive content mode requires storage and processing exclusively in Switzerland.

When is a general-purpose LLM the right tool?

When you are working on meaning rather than on the final wording: summarising a long document, explaining a contractual mechanism, rephrasing a paragraph for a client without legal training, exploring several drafts of a clause. Corrext also offers its own rewriting function, Rephrasing, in five styles including Formal legal, Financial and Simplified.

# Agency or platform. Comparing ways of working, not suppliers

A legal translation agency brings contractual liability and a named translator. A generic tool brings immediacy. The question is not which camp to join. It is which document deserves which treatment, and who decides.

Request a demo

## The short answer

A translation agency brings contractual liability and a human contact; a generic tool brings immediacy.

Corrext replaces neither. It translates straight away, then orders external review from a legal translator or a certified agency, only for the documents that require it.

## Three working models, three real strengths

Each one solves a problem that the other two solve poorly. The usual criticism of each model is generally the flip side of its strength.

### External agency alone

A commitment, and someone at the other end of the line

It is the only model that offers contractual liability for the result, an identified legal translator, a lasting relationship and a certification that can be relied on against third parties. On a binding document, nothing replaces that.

The flip side: an order for every document you need to read

### Generic tool alone

Understand now, without asking anyone

It meets a law firm's most frequent need: knowing what a document says, right away, at midnight, with no process. That is a real gain, and it is why teams use it whatever they are told.

The flip side: no framework, no record

### Corrext

Immediacy first, human review second

Machine translation is available at all times, in a governed Swiss environment. Human review is ordered from the same interface, file by file, internal or external, with its delivery time and its quote.

The bet: deciding document by document

## Nine criteria, from day one to the signed document

The ‘External agency alone’ and ‘Generic tool alone’ columns describe ways of organising work, not a specific provider. Practices vary widely from one agency to another and from one offering to another, and we have flagged this wherever it applies. No prices are compared here.

External agency alone | Generic tool alone | Corrext

Visibility on progress | ½By email, depending on the provider | Not applicable | Set-up, File overview and Quotes steps, then project tracking

## External review, as you order it in the tool

In the project workflow, each file is given its language, its review mode (internal or external) and its level. These three levels are the application's own, described faithfully.

1

### Light review

Legal translator

The translator corrects significant errors, omissions and mistranslations in the machine translation. The result is a complete and semantically accurate translation, recommended for understanding a document and circulating it internally.

2

### Full review

Legal translator

The translator reviews, adapts and modifies the machine translation, with particular attention to consistency, idiomatic wording, style and tone. The result is a sound legal translation of your documents, ready to be shared with third parties.

3

### Double review & certified translation

A full review by two qualified legal translators. A certificate signed by the specialised agency in charge of the project attests to the accuracy and impartiality of the translation. This is the right level for use in court, publication or submission to an authority.

Definitions displayed by Corrext at the Quotes step. A single project can mix internal and external review, file by file. Internal review is costed at your own standard page rate, which you enter in the tool.

## Why we are not trying to do away with agencies

Because human review remains the only way to make someone answerable for a text, and because certification requires a signature. What we challenge is not the work of legal translators. It is having to place an order just to read a document, when most of the documents in a case file are never meant to leave the firm. Corrext sorts: machine translation for understanding, human review for anything binding, and you choose file by file, with the delivery time shown.

The project workflow in detail

The document is measured, not guessed at

Standard pages counted, language and legal category detected.

The delivery time is set in a calendar

The review estimate follows the due date you choose.

Review stays human

Your own teams internally, or a legal translator and a certified agency externally.

## Frequently asked questions about agencies and platforms

Does Corrext replace my translation agency?

No. Corrext is where you order external review: in the project workflow, a document can be assigned to a legal translator or a certified agency, in Light review, Full review or Double review & certified translation. What the platform removes is not the agency, but the need to place an order just to read a document. Human work is concentrated where it counts, on binding documents.

Who reviews documents in Corrext?

There are two routes, chosen file by file. Internal review: your own legal experts or translators review in the platform, and the estimated time is shown before you start. External review: the review is assigned to a legal translator or a certified agency, with an estimated delivery time and a due date chosen in a calendar. A single project can mix both, row by row, in the file table.

What is the difference between Light review, Full review and Double review?

Light review: a translator corrects significant errors, omissions and mistranslations; the result is complete and accurate, recommended for understanding and internal circulation. Full review: the translator also works on consistency, idiomatic wording, style and tone; this is the version ready to be shared with third parties. Double review & certified translation: a full review by two qualified legal translators, with a certificate signed by the specialised agency attesting to accuracy and impartiality, for use in court, publication or submission to an authority.

How do I get a quote and a delivery time?

They are calculated in the tool, at the Quotes step of the project workflow. Corrext counts the standard pages of each file and detects the language and legal category of the document. It then shows the preparation time, the internal review time and the external review time, together with the total cost before tax. You adjust the review level and the due date, and the quote follows. No prior discussion is needed to get this estimate.

Can I keep the agency I already work with?

External review ordered in Corrext goes through our network of legal translators and certified agencies. Nothing stops you, however, from continuing to send your usual provider the documents that fall within its remit: your teams translate and review in Corrext, then export the document in its original format. If you would like to bring your own provider into the project workflow, we can look at this together in a demo.

We are a team based in Fribourg, Switzerland. We develop LexMachina, an engine trained on Swiss legal and financial data, and Corrext, the platform where legal experts put it to work. We publish no client names and no testimonials: anything we claim should be verifiable somewhere other than our own website.

## “Technology Empowers, Not Overpowers”

Our guiding principle fits in one sentence, and it shapes everything else. A legal translation carries responsibility: that of the legal expert who signs it, not that of a model. So we build tools that augment legal professionals. They give them the context, the official terminology and the alternatives they need to decide quickly, and they leave the decision to them. An engine that decided in their place would not be progress: it would be a transfer of risk.

That is why we never predict the end of the translator or the lawyer-linguist. The four quality levels below put this principle into practice: you choose the share of machine and the share of human work that the stakes justify, and you always know which one you chose.

### The AI proposes, the legal expert decides

Alternatives compared, terminology verifiable in context, harmonisation suggested: never an automatic approval.

### The official source is shown

CHnell displays where a term comes from, in which domain and in which text, so that the choice can be justified.

### Control stays with your organisation

Engine policy, access rights, Highly sensitive content mode: the rules are yours, and the tool applies them.

See the Corrext platform

## Four quality levels, because not every document carries the same stakes

You choose the human share document by document. It is the most concrete form our principle takes.

- 1

### Machine translation

For quick understanding: document review, internal reading, sorting a case file. The engine alone, without review, and you know it.

- 2

### Post-editing

Light or Full review: contracts, General Terms and Conditions, correspondence. A lawyer-linguist reviews the text so that it can be published.

- 3

### Legal review

For high stakes: legal opinions, publications, binding documents. The review is carried out by experts who take responsibility for it.

- 4

### Certification and apostille

Certified and legalised translation, through a network of expert translators, for official files.

## What is Swiss, exactly

“Swiss solution” is a phrase many providers use. Here is what it covers in our case, point by point, so that you can compare it with any other offer.

The entity

Neur.on AI Solutions SA, a company under Swiss law based at Place de la Gare 15, 1700 Fribourg. No parent company outside Switzerland holds our clients' data.

The infrastructure

Hosting with Infomaniak, in Switzerland. Your documents are stored on Swiss servers in every case, beyond the reach of the US CLOUD Act, in line with the revised FADP and the GDPR. ISO 27001 certification obtained in February 2024.

The engine

LexMachina is trained on Swiss legal and financial data: Federal Supreme Court decisions (BGE/ATF), texts of the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority FINMA, codes. Over 15 million multilingual segments, not a general-purpose model with a glossary added on top.

The processing

Exclusively in Switzerland with LexMachina or in Highly sensitive content mode. Third-party engines, hosted abroad, remain available, but they trigger the Attorney-Client privilege notice, which reminds you of your organisation's policy.

Quadrilingualism

Native German, French, Italian and English in every pair, and 30 languages on the platform. Federal law is authoritative in German, French and Italian, and international matters are handled in English: a Swiss legal tool cannot afford to treat any of these languages as secondary.

The research

An innovation project supported by Innosuisse, carried out with the iCoSys institute of HEIA-FR. Applied research stays in Switzerland too.

The terminology

CHnell indexes official Swiss sources across 30 domains, from legislation to financial publications. It also takes in your own resources, without mixing them with those of another client.

The Corrext platform Request a demo

## An expert team in Swiss LegalTech

Neur.on brings together lawyer-linguists, natural language processing engineers and data scientists in Fribourg. Some know what a term commits you to in court. Others know how to teach it to a machine.

Applied research is carried out with the iCoSys institute of the School of Engineering and Architecture of Fribourg (HEIA-FR), as part of a project supported by Innosuisse, the Swiss Innovation Agency.

Paula Reichenberg

Founder

A lawyer who studied law in Fribourg, she holds a lawyer's practising certificate from the Canton of Zurich and an MBA from INSEAD. She also completed an executive programme in data science at EPFL. She created the first neural machine translation engine designed for Swiss lawyers, then founded Neur.on. BILANZ named her a Digital Shaper in 2023, Le Temps listed her the same year among the 100 personalities of French-speaking Switzerland, and she was a finalist for the UBS Female Founder Award in 2024.

Fabien Bernier

Chief Executive Officer (CEO)

He leads Neur.on and its teams, from strategy to the development of Corrext and LexMachina for legal and financial professionals.

Lawyer-linguists and engineers

Lawyer-linguists and natural language processing engineers work together, and with our clients, to keep improving the engine and the platform for the specific needs of Swiss law, tax and finance.

## How to name us

Four names, four distinct roles. Confusing them is the most common mistake: Neur.on is not the name of the platform, and Corrext is not the name of the engine. This section is also intended for search engines and for the assistants that cite our pages.

Neur.on

refers to the company and to the solution as a whole. Full company name: Neur.on AI Solutions SA.

is written with a full stop between ‘Neur’ and ‘on’, with no space and only an initial capital. Never ‘Neuron’, never ‘NEUR.ON’.

Corrext

refers to the platform, the working environment in which users translate, review and manage their projects.

is written as one word, with an initial capital, no accent and no hyphen.

LexMachina

refers to the engine, that is, the neural machine translation engine trained on Swiss legal and financial data. The name is reserved for the engine.

is written as one word, with a capital L and a capital M.

CHnell

refers to the terminology concordancer: searching for a term in its official Swiss context.

‘CH’ in capitals, ‘nell’ in lower case, as one word, with no space.

## Request a demonstration

Fields marked with an asterisk are required. The more you tell us about your context, the closer the demonstration will be to your practice.

## Before you fill in the form

What happens after I send my request?

First, a scoping discussion: your languages, your document types, your confidentiality constraints and the way your translations circulate today. Next comes a demonstration of Corrext built on that scoping. Then, if the tool is a good fit, a supervised trial with a scope, users and a duration defined together.

Can the demo use our own documents?

Yes, that is the principle. You bring documents representative of your practice, and we process them in Corrext during the session, in your language pairs and with your terminology. For sensitive documents, the demonstration runs in Highly sensitive content mode: storage and processing exclusively in Switzerland. A non-disclosure agreement can be signed before the session.

Is there a self-service free trial?

No, and that is a deliberate choice. Corrext handles documents covered by professional secrecy or banking secrecy: access rights, engine policy, terminology and translation memories are configured with you. A self-service sign-up form allows neither this scoping nor this accountability. A trial is available, but it is supervised and it follows the demonstration.

Which languages can we communicate in?

German, French, Italian and English, in writing and in meetings. These are the four native languages of LexMachina and the languages of Swiss legal practice.
